It may also admit a fifth: that it means one who increases in goodness and righteousness.

﴿And remembers the name of his Lord and prays﴾. On this there are six aspects:

The first: that he affirms the oneness of Allah. This is related from Ibn 'Abbas.

The second: that he calls upon Him and turns to Him with desire.

The third: that he seeks forgiveness from Him and repents to Him.

The fourth: that he remembers Him in his heart during his prayer, so that he fears His punishment and hopes for His reward, so that the completeness of his prayer and his humility in it are in proportion to his fear and hope.

The fifth: that he mentions the name of his Lord with his tongue when he begins his prayer with the takbir, because the prayer is not valid except with that remembrance.

The sixth: that he begins every surah with ﴿In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful﴾.

The second: the prayer of the Eid. This is related from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri.

The third: that he performs a voluntary prayer after giving zakat. This is related from Abu al-Ahwas.

al-Dahhak mentioned that it was revealed concerning Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him.

﴿And the Hereafter is better and more enduring﴾. On this there are two aspects:

The second: what Qatadah said, that it is better in goodness and more enduring in permanence.

It may also admit a third aspect, by which the two aspects are combined: the Hereafter is better for the people of obedience and more enduring for the people of Paradise.

﴿Indeed, this is in the former scrolls﴾. On this there are three ssayings: The first: meaning that the Hereafter is better and more enduring is in the former scrolls. This is said by Qatadah.

The second: that what Allah related in this surah is from the former scrolls.

One: that by it is meant the disbelievers, so its interpretation is: rather, you prefer the worldly life over the Hereafter.

The second: that by it is meant the Muslims, so its interpretation is: they prefer seeking more of the world in order to seek more reward.

﴿And the Hereafter is better and more enduring﴾. On this there are two aspects:

One: it is better for the believer than the world, and more enduring in terms of recompense.

The second: what Qatadah said, that it is better in goodness and more enduring in permanence.

It may also admit a third aspect, by which the two aspects are combined: the Hereafter is better for the people of obedience and more enduring for the people of Paradise.

﴿Indeed, this is in the former scrolls﴾. On this there are three ssayings: The first: meaning that the Hereafter is better and more enduring is in the former scrolls. This is said by Qatadah.

The second: that what Allah related in this surah is from the former scrolls.

The third: that it refers to all the books of Allah. Wahb ibn Munabbih related in al-Mubtada' that the total of the books which Allah sent down to His prophets is one hundred and four scrolls and four books. Of these, thirty-five scrolls were sent down to Shith ibn Adam, fifty scrolls to Idris, and twenty scrolls to Ibrahim. He sent the Torah to Musa, the Psalms to Dawud, the Gospel to 'Isa, and the Furqan to Muhammad, upon them be peace.

He wrote: ﴿Certainly the one who purifies himself will prosper﴾. On this there are four interpretations (ta'wil):

The first: it means one who purifies himself from polytheism through faith. This is related from Ibn 'Abbas.

The second: it means one whose righteous deeds are pure and growing. This is related from al-Hasan and al-Rabi'.

He did not mention the third; see the note in the edition, p. 44.

The fourth: it means that he intended the zakat on all wealth. This is related from Abu al-Ahwas.

It may also admit a fifth: that it means one who increases in goodness and righteousness.

﴿And remembers the name of his Lord and prays﴾. On this there are six aspects:

The first: that he affirms the oneness of Allah. This is related from Ibn 'Abbas.

The second: that he calls upon Him and turns to Him with desire.

The third: that he seeks forgiveness from Him and repents to Him.

The fourth: that he remembers Him in his heart during his prayer, so that he fears His punishment and hopes for His reward, so that the completeness of his prayer and his humility in it are in proportion to his fear and hope.

The fifth: that he mentions the name of his Lord with his tongue when he begins his prayer with the takbir, because the prayer is not valid except with that remembrance.

The sixth: that he begins every surah with ﴿In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful﴾.
